card.text: One quasar seen four times: a nearer galaxy's gravity bends its light into four images.

sources.label: ESA/Hubble potw1204a: ESA/Hubble & NASA
sources.locator: caption: the galaxy's powerful gravity acts as a lens that bends and amplifies the light from the quasar behind it, producing four images of the distant object

sources.label: NASA/IPAC Extragalactic Database (NED), Einstein Cross: position from 1994AJ....107..461B, redshift from 2017A&A...600A..79A
sources.locator: NED preferred values of Einstein Cross: RA 340.1261289°, Dec 3.358619494° (1994AJ....107..461B); redshift 1.695 (2017A&A...600A..79A)

sources.label: Planck Collaboration (2020), Planck 2018 results VI, A&A 641, A6; Astropy Planck18
sources.locator: z = 1.695: comoving distance 4,826 Mpc, lookback time 9.96 Gyr, age 3830 Myr

introduction.text: Hubble's view: the four points are one quasar, and the faint glow between them is the core of the nearer galaxy that bends its light. The picture is flat and has no depth.

sources.label: ESA/Hubble potw1204a: ESA/Hubble & NASA
sources.locator: Seeing quadruple; Hubble; the page lists no filters

optical.title: The Einstein Cross from Hubble
optical.summary: Four images of one quasar around the core of the galaxy that lenses it. A flat picture, with no depth.
